task_brief: Day 6 of "Portfolio and Public or Private Exhibition" (unit 6, grade 8) is a guided practice (second pass) on future arts pathways. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Complete a polished cross-arts portfolio and exhibition, performance, screening, or private defense. Today's work contributes to that by handling future arts pathways at the guided practice b stage, against the unit's wider topics of portfolio selection, professional presentation, artist statements, and audience and venue. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Complete a second supported pass on future arts pathways with the reference put away. Make two fresh short studies from memory and judgement, then set them beside the first pass. Where the unassisted work differs, decide which version better achieves the effect and write the reason in terms of the actual work, not preference alone. Revisit the move you flagged as unrepeatable and report honestly whether it held. Sharing remains private; no recording, photograph, or performance for an audience is required. Use the attached earlier-pass substitute when prior work is unavailable, hide it as directed, and finish both unassisted studies before checking. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about future arts pathways, and it belongs to "Portfolio and Public or Private Exhibition", which also covers separate topics such as portfolio selection. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about future arts pathways; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.

guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for future arts pathways fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. The supporting adult may ask "what supports that move?" after a step but should not supply the step. Where the unscaffolded attempt diverges from the scaffolded one, the divergence itself is the thing to examine, not something to erase.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting future arts pathways.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for future arts pathways follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for future arts pathways, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for future arts pathways works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of future arts pathways, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking future arts pathways mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply future arts pathways under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on future arts pathways rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
